evidence: The resolver is org-membership gated: resolve_org_github_login_to_users (products/signals/backend/report_generation/resolve_reviewers.py:304-332) only considers candidates from _candidate_user_ids_for_org_and_logins (355-384), whose every branch is filtered by the OrganizationMembership subquery `mid_sq`. Every production path that revokes access deletes that membership row: org-member removal via the API (posthog/api/organization_member.py:256-278 -> User.leave) and User.leave itself (posthog/models/user.py:561-566, `membership.delete()`); SCIM deprovisioning (ee/api/scim/user.py:267-295 PUT active=false -> deactivate() -> _leave_organization(); PATCH handle_replace 'active' false -> deactivate() at 308-322) also removes the membership and never sets User.is_active=False (the SCIM_USER_ATTR_MAP 'is_active' entry at ee/api/scim/views.py:171 is bypassed by the 'active' special case). No non-test code sets User.is_active=False (grep over posthog/, ee/, products/ finds only unrelated models; the only path is the staff-only Django admin form, posthog/admin/admins/user_admin.py:97). So for a departed user both the initial receiver (receivers.py:111-113, 202-205) and the webhook resolver (receivers.py:151-153) already return None, and the finding's 'enable the toggle, lose access, still authorize approvals' scenario does not reach process_inbox_pr_review (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110) or the carve-out (tasks.py:201-206). The residual window is an org member removed from a private project (ACCESS_CONTROL + AccessControl project=none, posthog/models/team/team.py:1116-1160) or a staff-admin is_active flip with the membership left in place. That is reachable but it is not an authorization gap: the approval's security invariants are task linkage, repo-native bot authorship, and the team's synced+enabled StamphogRepoConfig (products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:80-112; tasks.py:152-207, 1131-1150), the approval is posted by the App, and the acting reviewer's project access never underpins it; the toggle is a per-user consent/budget opt-in (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:275-280). The org-member (not project-access) resolution is a deliberate mirror of the Inbox 'For you' filter, Slack notifications (products/signals/backend/slack_inbox_notifications.py:184) and the artefact views (products/signals/backend/views.py:2134, 2318) -- receivers.py:162-165 documents that choice -- so intersecting with all_users_with_access() would make this one surface diverge from its siblings. 'Cannot clear the toggle after losing access' is true only for the private-project case (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:84-105 is project-scoped via TeamAndOrgViewSetMixin, posthog/api/routing.py:296-299) and holds for every per-user preference in a project the user left. Existing tests cover the org-membership boundary (products/signals/backend/test/test_resolve_reviewers.py:90-110; products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:38-45, 379-396) but not the private-project residual.
notes: Would flip to consider/should_fix if a production path set User.is_active=False while keeping the OrganizationMembership (today only Django admin does), or if the acting reviewer's identity were what made the approval legitimate (e.g. the App posted on the user's behalf, or the approval satisfied a branch-protection rule keyed to that reviewer). Adjacent but out of this finding's scope: the ReviewHog inbox leg runs sandbox work as the acting user (receivers.py:262-267 user_id=acting_user_id -> activities.py:716-727), so a staff-deactivated acting reviewer would hit the sandbox-credential hang the label trigger guards against (products/review_hog/backend/api/trigger.py:56-64, 160-170); that is a functional ReviewHog-leg concern, not the Stamphog authorization gap claimed here.
